title: Git Add Command
overview: The git add command moves changes from the working directory to the staging area before committing.

example.title: Add Files
example.content:
git add filename

or

git add .

title: Git Commit Command
overview: A commit saves the staged changes as a snapshot in the Git repository history.

title: Git Log Command
overview: Git log displays the history of commits made in a repository.

title: Git Diff Command
overview: Git diff shows the differences between files before committing changes.

title: Git Remove Command
overview: Git rm removes files from the working directory and stages the removal.

title: Git Restore Command
overview: Git restore is used to discard changes or restore files to previous states.

title: Git Ignore File
overview: The .gitignore file tells Git which files or folders should not be tracked.

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned essential Git commands used for adding, saving, checking, and managing project changes.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ git add stages changes.
✔ git commit saves changes.
✔ git log shows history.
✔ .gitignore excludes files.
